newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo govt to take DKB off public fund management.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo govt to take DKB off public fund management.

text.p: The Tokyo metropolitan government is planning to remove Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) from management of public funds from May 30, an official of the metropolitan government Treasury Department said on Thursday.
But he added: "It shouldn't really be considered a penalty. We just thought it was better at present that DKB be removed from public fund management."

He declined to specify how long this would last or whether further measures would be taken against DKB, adding that it depended on investigations currently being carried out against the bank as well as how monetary authorities will react.
An official in the metropolitan government's bond section said no decision has been reached as yet on whether to exclude DKB from bond underwriting.
"We have to wait and see what steps may be carried out by the government before deciding this," she added.
The Tokyo metropolitan government is planning to issue 540 billion yen worth of public placement bonds in 1997/98.
DKB's current share in the underwriting syndicate for the metropolitan government's bonds is 7.2 percent.
Top executives of DKB resigned last Friday when the bank admitted it had links to a racketeer at the centre of a widening saga of dubious deals and illegal payoffs involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
DKB said the bank had made a total of 26 billion yen in loans to Yoshinori Koike, the younger brother of a racketeer at the heart of the Nomura scandal.
